title: Data policies (DLP) for Copilot Studio agents
notes: 2026-11-16: taken offline; the grace for pages published before the check existed is off
summary: Hold: the page overstates endpoint filtering for custom connectors and MCP servers, and omits the knowledge-source and channel restrictions on Purview DLP. It also confuses the January 2025 enforcement announcement with the end of enforcement exemptions in March 2025.

claims.where: What a data policy does: first sentence
claims.claim: Power Platform data policies, also called DLP policies, classify connectors into Business, Non-business and Blocked groups.
claims.quote:
In the Power Platform admin center, you can classify Copilot Studio connectors within a data policy under the following data groups:
- Business
- Non-business
- Blocked

claims.where: What a data policy does; Operating pattern: environment-scoped policies
claims.claim: Data policies can be scoped to a tenant or to specific environments.
claims.quote: Data policies can be defined at the tenant level (applying to all environments in a tenant) or for one or more specific environments.

claims.where: What a data policy does: apps and flows cannot combine connector groups
claims.claim: An app or flow cannot combine Business and Non-business connectors.
claims.quote: makers can't create an app or flow that uses both the SharePoint and Gmail connectors.
claims.fix: Add the Microsoft pages relied on but absent from sources, together: https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/dlp-connector-classification ; https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/wp-data-loss-prevention ; https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-agent-status ; https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/authoring-agent-status ; https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/add-tools-custom-agent ; https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/managed-environment-sharing-limits ; https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/ai-copilot-studio . These substantiate connector classification, virtual connectors, readiness and guidance, credential selection, sharing and Purview applicability.

claims.where: What a data policy does: agents cannot combine connector groups
claims.claim: An agent cannot combine connectors from different data groups.
claims.quote: In a data policy, the connectors must be in the same data group because data can't be shared among connectors that are in different groups.

claims.where: What a data policy does: Blocked connector
claims.claim: A connector classified as Blocked cannot be used.
claims.quote: Classify connectors that you want to keep from being used at all across one or more environments as Blocked.

claims.where: What a data policy does: Since January 2025
claims.claim: Mandatory data policy enforcement on every agent without opt-in has applied since January 2025.
claims.quote: Since March 2025, agents can't be exempted from data policy enforcement. It's no longer possible to exempt agents with a PowerShell command.
claims.fix: Replace the date with 'Since March 2025, agents cannot be exempted from data policy enforcement.' January 6, 2025 was the MC973179 announcement date, not the documented date exemptions ended.

claims.where: What a data policy does: every agent without an opt-in
claims.claim: Data policy enforcement now applies to all tenants and agents without the earlier opt-in exemption.
claims.quote: Agent data policy enforcement exemption is no longer supported. Agents that were previously exempted from data policy enforcement are all subject to enforcement.

claims.where: What a data policy does: maker errors
claims.claim: Agents violating data policies show errors in the maker experience.
claims.quote: Copilot Studio supports data policy enforcement in real time. Agent makers and users see error messages for any data policy violation.

claims.where: What a data policy does: publication blocked
claims.claim: An agent violating a data policy cannot be published.
claims.quote: When a data policy violation occurs, the Publish button becomes unavailable.

claims.where: What a data policy does: already-published agents
claims.claim: Already-published agents fail when they attempt to use a capability blocked by data policy.
claims.quote: Any resources that are running and attempting to use an inactive connection, action, trigger, or MCP server that is blocked, fail at runtime.

claims.where: summary; What a data policy does: capabilities as connectors
claims.claim: Copilot Studio exposes agent capabilities through connectors so data policies govern tools, knowledge, channels and triggers.
claims.quote:
including:
- Maker and user authentication
- Knowledge sources
- Actions, connectors, and Azure Bot Service skills
- HTTP requests
- Publication to channels
- Azure Monitor Application Insights
- Triggers

claims.where: Connector names that govern agent capabilities: authentication row
claims.claim: Blocking Chat without Microsoft Entra ID authentication in Copilot Studio prevents publishing agents without authentication.
claims.quote: To prevent agent makers from publishing agents that don't require authentication, configure a data policy that blocks the connector Chat without Microsoft Entra ID authentication in Copilot Studio.

claims.where: Connector names that govern agent capabilities: HTTP row
claims.claim: Blocking the HTTP connector prevents makers from publishing agents that make HTTP requests.
claims.quote: To prevent agent makers from publishing agents that make HTTP requests, configure a data policy that blocks the HTTP connector.

claims.where: Connector names that govern agent capabilities: HTTP endpoint filtering
claims.claim: HTTP supports endpoint filtering with allow or deny lists.
claims.quote: Alternatively, if you want to allow or deny specific HTTP endpoints instead of blocking all HTTP calls, use endpoint filtering.
claims.fix: Mark HTTP connector endpoint filtering as preview, as explicitly stated at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/connector-endpoint-filtering . Its HTTP section documents ordered Allow and Deny URL patterns.

claims.where: Connector names that govern agent capabilities: Direct Line row
claims.claim: Blocking Direct Line channels in Copilot Studio prevents publishing to web, mobile and custom Direct Line channels.
claims.quote: Direct Line channels in Copilot Studio (applies to the Demo website, custom websites, mobile app, and other Direct Line channels)

claims.where: Connector names that govern agent capabilities: Teams and Microsoft 365 row
claims.claim: Microsoft Teams + Microsoft 365 Channel in Copilot Studio governs publication to Teams and Microsoft 365 Copilot.
claims.quote: | Publishing to the Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Teams channel. | Microsoft Teams + Microsoft 365 Channel in Copilot Studio |

claims.where: Connector names that govern agent capabilities: corresponding channel connector, SharePoint
claims.claim: A corresponding channel connector can block publication to SharePoint.
claims.quote: | Publishing to the SharePoint channel. | SharePoint channel in Copilot Studio |

claims.where: Connector names that govern agent capabilities: corresponding channel connector, WhatsApp
claims.claim: A corresponding channel connector can block publication to WhatsApp.
claims.quote: | Publishing to the WhatsApp channel. | WhatsApp channel in Copilot Studio |

claims.where: Connector names that govern agent capabilities: corresponding channel connector, Facebook
claims.claim: A corresponding channel connector can block publication to Facebook.
claims.quote: | Publishing to the Facebook channel. | Facebook channel in Copilot Studio |

claims.where: Connector names that govern agent capabilities: corresponding channel connector, Customer Service
claims.claim: A corresponding channel connector can block publication to Dynamics 365 Customer Service.
claims.quote: | Publishing to the Dynamics 365 Customer Service channel. | Omnichannel in Copilot Studio |

claims.where: Connector names that govern agent capabilities: event triggers row
claims.claim: Blocking the Microsoft Copilot Studio connector prevents use of event triggers for autonomous agents.
claims.quote: To prevent agent makers from adding event triggers to their agents or running automated evaluations by using an authenticated account, configure a data policy that blocks the Microsoft Copilot Studio connector.

claims.where: Connector names that govern agent capabilities: authenticated evaluations row
claims.claim: Blocking the Microsoft Copilot Studio connector prevents automated evaluations using authenticated accounts.
claims.quote: | Using event triggers in Copilot Studio agents or running automated evaluations using authenticated accounts. | Microsoft Copilot Studio |

claims.where: Connector names that govern agent capabilities: skills row
claims.claim: Blocking Skills with Copilot Studio prevents use of Azure Bot Service skills.
claims.quote: To prevent agent makers from publishing agents that use Azure Bot Service skills, configure a data policy that blocks the Skills with Copilot Studio connector.

claims.where: Connector names that govern agent capabilities: telemetry row
claims.claim: Application Insights in Copilot Studio governs connecting agents to Application Insights for telemetry.
claims.quote: | Connecting agents with Application Insights. | Application Insights in Copilot Studio |

claims.where: Connector names that govern agent capabilities: Power Platform tools row
claims.claim: Data policies govern Power Platform connector tools through the specific prebuilt or custom connectors.
claims.quote: | Using Power Platform connectors as tools in Copilot Studio agents. | Many prebuilt and custom connectors |

claims.where: summary; Connector names that govern agent capabilities: MCP tools
claims.claim: Blocking Power Platform connectors also blocks tools in connected MCP servers that rely on those connectors.
claims.quote: Blocking Power Platform connectors also blocks access to tools in connected MCP servers, which rely on Power Platform connectors for connectivity.

claims.where: Connector names that govern agent capabilities: every channel blocked
claims.claim: Agents cannot be published if every channel is blocked.
claims.quote: If all channels for the agent are blocked by data policies, you can't publish your agent.

claims.where: Connector names that govern agent capabilities: allowed channel not configured
claims.claim: Agents cannot be published if no unblocked channel is configured.
claims.quote: If makers don't configure their agents for a channel that isn't blocked (Direct Line channels are allowed by default), or if the administrators don't allow any channel, agents can't be published.

claims.where: Connector names that govern agent capabilities: Direct Line default
claims.claim: Direct Line channels are allowed by default.
claims.quote: Direct Line channels are allowed by default

claims.where: How restrictions appear to makers: disabled capabilities
claims.claim: Blocked connectors and channels appear disabled in the authoring interface.
claims.quote: a blocked connector appears disabled when a maker adds tools to an agent, and a restricted channel appears disabled when a maker attempts to add a channel while publishing an agent.

claims.where: How restrictions appear to makers: hover explanation
claims.claim: Makers can hover over blocked capabilities to see why they are restricted.
claims.quote: Makers can hover over the unavailable capability to view information about why it's restricted.

claims.where: How restrictions appear to makers: Review pane
claims.claim: The Review pane lists blocking issues and warnings.
claims.quote: The Review panel lists issues ordered by severity: Blocking issues first, followed by Warnings.
claims.fix: Identify the harness: the Microsoft Copilot harness has the Review panel described at this URL. For standard-harness agents, describe Overview > Agent status > Review and flag that readiness experience as preview, as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/authoring-agent-status .

claims.where: How restrictions appear to makers; Operating pattern: custom guidance message
claims.claim: Administrators can set a custom guidance message and contact details for makers blocked by policy.
claims.quote:
Custom guidance message (preview)

As an admin, you can set an environment-level guidance message for users when they encounter a blocked or disabled capability. This plain-text message replaces the default Contact your admin prompt.
claims.fix: Label custom guidance messages as preview in both their description and the operating-pattern recommendation. Distinguish this environment/environment-group Maker guidance feature from the existing tenant-wide data-policy contact email and Learn more link.

claims.where: How restrictions appear to makers: DlpViolationError
claims.claim: Publishing an agent that violates a data policy produces a DlpViolationError.
claims.quote:
| errorDescription | At least one connector here has been blocked by your admin |
| $kind | DlpViolationError |

claims.where: How restrictions appear to makers: violationType
claims.claim: The error's violationType identifies the cause, for example BlockedConnector.
claims.quote:
| errorDescription | At least one connector here has been blocked by your admin |
| $kind | DlpViolationError |
| violationType | BlockedConnector |

claims.where: Working with the rest of the control set: Endpoint filtering
claims.claim: Connector endpoint filtering narrows both HTTP and custom connectors to specific hosts.
claims.quote:
it's exclusively available for the following connectors:
- HTTP
- HTTP with Microsoft Entra ID (AD)
- HTTP Webhook
- SQL Server (includes using SQL Server Connector to access Azure Synapse data warehouse)
- Azure Blob Storage
- SMTP
- Browser Automation
- UI Automation
claims.fix: Separate the controls: HTTP connector endpoint filtering is preview and evaluates static design-time endpoints, not dynamically bound runtime endpoints. Custom connectors are classified by Host URL patterns in tenant-level data policies, as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/dlp-connector-classification#tenant-level-data-policies ; do not describe that classification as the same endpoint-filtering feature.

claims.where: Working with the rest of the control set: pin an MCP server
claims.claim: Endpoint filtering can pin an MCP server without blocking its connector.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio MCP endpoint filtering. Opened connector-endpoint-filtering, dlp-connector-classification, admin-data-loss-prevention and wp-data-loss-prevention; none states that HTTP endpoint rules pin an MCP server while leaving its connector available.
claims.fix: Remove 'which is how you pin an MCP server or API without blocking the connector'. State instead that blocking an MCP server's underlying connector blocks its tools; custom connector Host URL classification and HTTP static-endpoint rules are distinct controls with different scopes.

claims.where: Working with the rest of the control set: Credential controls
claims.claim: Credential configuration decides whose identity a permitted connector tool uses.
claims.quote: Authentication: Select whether to use the user's (End user) or maker's (Maker-provided) credentials for the tool. By default, user authentication applies.

claims.where: Working with the rest of the control set: Sharing limits
claims.claim: Managed Environments sharing limits govern how broadly agents can be shared.
claims.quote: In managed environments, admins can limit how broadly users can share canvas apps, flows, and agents.

claims.where: Working with the rest of the control set: Purview DLP
claims.claim: Purview DLP at the Microsoft 365 Copilot location governs what content agents may process without knowledge-source or channel qualifications.
claims.quote: When the knowledge source is SharePoint, a DLP policy scoped to the Microsoft 365 Copilot location can restrict agents built in Copilot Studio for Microsoft Teams, SharePoint, and Microsoft 365 Copilot from processing sensitive content based on a specified sensitivity label.
claims.fix: Replace with: 'For SharePoint knowledge sources, a Purview DLP policy scoped to the Microsoft 365 Copilot location can restrict Copilot Studio agents for Teams, SharePoint and Microsoft 365 Copilot from processing content with a specified sensitivity label. This is separate from connector governance.'

claims.where: Operating pattern: review connector dependency insights
claims.claim: Administrators can review connector dependencies used by agents to assess data movement risk before applying governance controls.
claims.quote: Admins can review connector dependencies used by agents to understand data movement risk and apply governance controls before deployment.

claims.where: Operating pattern: connector dependency insights in the Power Platform admin center
claims.claim: Copilot Studio connector dependency insights are available in the Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio connector dependency admin center; site:learn.microsoft.com/power-platform connector dependencies agents; Copilot Studio dependency insights. Opened security-and-governance and admin-data-loss-prevention; neither locates that view in the portal.
claims.fix: Remove the unverified portal location. For an actionable documented alternative, direct makers and admins to check published agent status and download policy-violation reports from the agent's Channels page in Copilot Studio, as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-dlp-troubleshooting#identify-agents-in-violation-of-a-data-policy .

claims.where: Operating pattern: controls named without governance control rows
claims.claim: The operating checklist tells administrators to configure controls that have no corresponding governance controls rows.
claims.quote:
Start from the default environment: block channels and connectors citizen makers should not use; allow Teams and Microsoft 365 if that is your intended surface.
Set a custom guidance message so blocked makers get your request process, not a generic prompt.
claims.fix: Add governance controls rows for environment/tenant data policies controlling connectors and channels, and for custom maker guidance. Use the documented Power Platform admin center paths in admin-data-loss-prevention and authoring-agent-status respectively; flag Maker guidance as preview.
